answer: A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, as each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The canyon cap is enforced at intake and anchor makes public the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a cipher tag. That is 27 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
